root_cause.text: `net/core/dev.c` reused a `flow_id` computed in `get_rps_cpu()` when indexing the per-receive-queue RPS `flow_table` in `set_rps_cpu()`, but that index is only valid for the specific queue/table size and can become stale or out of bounds if the RPS table sizes differ or change.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `flow_id` parameter from `set_rps_cpu()`, adds `flow_id = rfs_slot(hash, flow_table);` inside `set_rps_cpu()` right before `flow_table->flows[flow_id]`, and the commit message says the blamed commit “made the assumption that the RPS table for each receive queue would have the same size, and that it would not change,” which “risk[s] out-of-bound access and/or crashes.”

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 97bcc5b6f45425ac56fb04b0893cdaa607ec7e45
Author: Krishna Kumar <krikku@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Aug 25 08:40:04 2025 +0530

    net: Prevent RPS table overwrite of active flows
    
    This patch fixes an issue where two different flows on the same RXq
    produce the same hash resulting in continuous flow overwrites.
    
    Flow #1: A packet for Flow #1 comes in, kernel calls the steering
             function. The driver gives back a filter id. The kernel saves
             this filter
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the new anti-overwrite logic, not the vulnerable construct described in the root cause. In `set_rps_cpu()` it computes `hash = skb_get_hash(skb);` and then `flow_id = rfs_slot(hash, flow_table);`, but before programming a new filter it checks the existing slot: `if (READ_ONCE(tmp_rflow->filter) != RPS_NO_FILTER) { if (rps_flow_is_active(tmp_rflow, flow_table, tmp_cpu)) { if (hash != READ_ONCE(tmp_rflow->hash) || next_cpu == tmp_cpu) goto out; } }`. This means it no longer blindly reuses the slot just because `flow_id` was computed; it avoids overwriting an active flow unless the hash/CPU conditions allow it. It also stores the hash with `WRITE_ONCE(rflow->hash, hash);`, which is part of the fix. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent and the fix is present.
